_note: Generated by tools/build-clips.py from wisegraph/. Teacher records for speakers with talks on the site.

Ajahn Nyanamoli Thero.tagline: Right view, sense restraint and the danger in sensuality, straight from the suttas.
Ajahn Nyanamoli Thero.bio: Founder of Hillside Hermitage; ordained in the Thai Theravāda tradition and a monk since 2005, teaching from the early suttas.

Bhikkhu Anīgha.bio: Monk of Hillside Hermitage and student of Ajahn Nyanamoli; often his partner in the recorded discussions.

Thaniyo Thero.bio: Monk of Hillside Hermitage who prepares the condensed transcripts of its talks.

Sister Medhini.bio: Nun practising under Ajahn Nyanamoli's guidance; writer for Hillside Hermitage.

Jiddu Krishnamurti.bio: Indian speaker raised by the Theosophical Society, who left it in 1929 to teach that truth is a pathless land; much archive footage survives.

specials.title: The Ending of Time (with David Bohm)
Truth is a Pathless Land (dissolution speech)

Ramana Maharshi.bio: Sage of Arunachala who taught self-enquiry: ask 'Who am I?'.

Nisargadatta Maharaj.bio: Bombay teacher of the Inchegeri line whose dialogues in I Am That made 'I am' the doorway to the Absolute.

specials.title: Consciousness and the Absolute: The Final Talks (ed. Jean Dunn)

Rudolf Steiner.bio: Austrian esotericist who left Theosophy to found Anthroposophy, a path of spiritual science.

Rupert Spira.bio: English potter turned teacher of the direct path, who points to awareness as the one reality behind all experience; a student of Francis Lucille.

specials.title: You Are the Happiness You Seek

Francis Lucille.bio: French-born non-dual teacher in the line of Jean Klein, known for dialogues that test every claim against direct experience.

Mooji.bio: Jamaican-born teacher of self-enquiry who met Papaji in Lucknow in 1993 and now teaches from Monte Sahaja in Portugal.

specials.title: Vaster Than Sky, Greater Than Space

Adyashanti.bio: American teacher trained in Zen who now teaches awakening outside any one tradition through his Open Gate Sangha.

Swami Tadatmananda.bio: American-born monk and teacher of Advaita Vedanta and meditation at the Arsha Bodha Center in New Jersey, a disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati.

specials.title: The Inner Journey: A Course in Meditation

Christopher Wallis (Hareesh).bio: Sanskrit scholar and practitioner of classical Śaiva Tantra who translates and teaches the non-dual texts of Kashmir Shaivism for modern practice.

Swami Lakshmanjoo.bio: Kashmiri master regarded as the last living holder of the oral tradition of Kashmir Shaivism; his recorded teachings are kept by the Lakshmanjoo Academy.

specials.title: Vijñāna Bhairava: The Practice of Centring Awareness

David Godman.bio: English writer who has lived at Tiruvannamalai since the 1970s and has written the standard books on Ramana Maharshi, his devotees and Papaji.

specials.title: Be As You Are: The Teachings of Sri Ramana Maharshi
Living by the Words of Bhagavan

Swami Sarvapriyananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and head of the Vedanta Society of New York, known for clear lectures on Advaita Vedanta and consciousness.

Brother Chidananda.bio: President and spiritual head of Self-Realization Fellowship / Yogoda Satsanga Society of India since 2017, teaching Yogananda's Kriya Yoga path.

specials.title: SRF Convocation and online meditation talks

Sri Mrinalini Mata.bio: Direct disciple of Paramahansa Yogananda, trained by him to edit his writings, and fourth president of Self-Realization Fellowship.

specials.title: Manifesting Divine Consciousness in Daily Life

Sri Daya Mata.bio: Direct disciple of Paramahansa Yogananda who led Self-Realization Fellowship as its president for more than fifty years.

Brother Anandamoy.bio: Swiss-born monk and direct disciple of Paramahansa Yogananda who lectured for Self-Realization Fellowship for decades.

Brother Bhumananda.bio: Monk of the Self-Realization Fellowship order who gives talks and guided practice on Yogananda's teachings.

Brother Achalananda.bio: Monk of the Self-Realization Fellowship order who gives talks and guided practice on Yogananda's teachings.

Brother Satyananda.bio: Monk of the Self-Realization Fellowship order who gives talks and guided practice on Yogananda's teachings.

Brother Kamalananda.bio: Monk of the Self-Realization Fellowship order who gives talks and guided practice on Yogananda's teachings.

Brother Prafullananda.bio: Monk of the Self-Realization Fellowship order who gives talks and guided practice on Yogananda's teachings.

Sister Usha.bio: Nun of the Self-Realization Fellowship order who gives short talks on Yogananda's teachings.

Swami Sarvadevananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and minister of the Vedanta Society of Southern California in Hollywood.

Swami Mahayogananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of Southern California who speaks on Vedanta, near-death experience and rebirth.

Swami Satyamayananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order whose talks are published by the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

Swami Atmaghanananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order whose talks are published by the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

Swami Atmavidyananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order whose talks are published by the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

Swami Vedarupananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order whose talks are published by the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

Pravrajika Vidyaprana.bio: Nun of the Sarada Convent of the Vedanta Society of Southern California who answers questions on Vedanta.

Dr. Venkat S. Ramanan.bio: President of Sri Ramanasramam in Tiruvannamalai (also known as Dr. Anand Ramanan), who speaks on Ramana Maharshi's teaching at the ashram's celebrations.

Sri Nochur Venkataraman.bio: Vedanta teacher from Kerala known for long talk series on Ramana Maharshi's poems, several given in English at Sri Ramanasramam.

Aparna Krishnamoorthy.bio: Speaker on the Advaitic meaning of Ramana Maharshi's hymns, in a talk published by Sri Ramanasramam.

Ganapathi Raman.bio: Devotee of Ramana Maharshi interviewed for Sri Ramanasramam's devotee-interview series.

Dhiruben Patel.bio: Devotee of Ramana Maharshi whose recollections were recorded by Sri Ramanasramam.

Dr. Santa Ramachandran.bio: Devotee who recalls moments with Ramana Maharshi in a recording published by Sri Ramanasramam.

Mangalam Kalyanam.bio: Granddaughter of Niranjanananda Swami, the ashram's first sarvadhikari and Ramana Maharshi's younger brother, recorded by Sri Ramanasramam.

Sethulakshmi.bio: Devotee of Ramana Maharshi interviewed for Sri Ramanasramam's devotee-interview series.

Swami Dayananda Saraswati.bio: Teacher of traditional Advaita Vedanta who founded the Arsha Vidya Gurukulams and trained Swami Tadatmananda among many others.

Ajahn Brahm.tagline: Jhāna, kindness and rebirth, taught with stories and laughter.
Ajahn Brahm.bio: British-born monk trained under Ajahn Chah in Thailand, abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery and spiritual director of the Buddhist Society of Western Australia.
Ajahn Brahm.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

specials.title: Opening the Door of Your Heart

Ajahn Sumedho.tagline: Intuitive awareness and the deathless, here and now.
Ajahn Sumedho.bio: American-born senior Western disciple of Ajahn Chah who founded Chithurst and Amaravati monasteries in England and led them for decades.
Ajahn Sumedho.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Amaro.tagline: Forest-tradition practice with a light touch.
Ajahn Amaro.bio: English monk ordained in Ajahn Chah's lineage, co-founder of Abhayagiri in California and later abbot of Amaravati.
Ajahn Amaro.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

specials.title: The Island: An Anthology of the Buddha's Teachings on Nibbāna

Ajahn Pasanno.tagline: Steady forest wisdom on death, fear and letting go.
Ajahn Pasanno.bio: Canadian monk who trained with Ajahn Chah, served as abbot of Wat Pah Nanachat and then co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery.
Ajahn Pasanno.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

specials.title: The Island: An Anthology of the Buddha's Teachings on Nibbāna

Thanissaro Bhikkhu.tagline: Breath, kamma and skilful action, one evening talk at a time.
Thanissaro Bhikkhu.bio: American monk of the Thai forest Kammaṭṭhāna tradition, abbot of Metta Forest Monastery and a prolific translator of the Pāli suttas.
Thanissaro Bhikkhu.traditionLabel: Dhammayut forest line (Ajahn Mun → Maha Boowa / Ajaan Lee)

Thich Nhat Hanh.tagline: Interbeing, no birth and no death, and the art of mindful living.
Thich Nhat Hanh.bio: Vietnamese Zen monk, poet and peace activist who founded the Plum Village tradition and taught mindfulness and interbeing worldwide.

specials.title: The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching

Shunryu Suzuki.bio: Japanese Sōtō priest who founded San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara; his recorded talks shaped Western Zen practice.

Shohaku Okumura.tagline: Reading Dōgen closely, sitting zazen simply.
Shohaku Okumura.bio: Japanese Sōtō Zen priest and translator of Dōgen, a student of Kōshō Uchiyama, and founding teacher of Sanshin Zen Community in Indiana.

Joan Halifax.tagline: Compassion at the edge: dying, care and engaged practice.
Joan Halifax.bio: American Zen teacher, anthropologist and founding abbot of Upaya Zen Center, known for her work on care for the dying.

Henry Shukman.bio: British poet and novelist who became a Sanbō Zen teacher and guiding teacher of Mountain Cloud Zen Center in Santa Fe.

Brad Warner.bio: American Sōtō Zen priest, author and former punk bassist who received transmission from Gudō Nishijima.

Shinge Roshi.tagline: Rinzai sesshin talks from Dai Bosatsu.
Shinge Roshi.bio: Shinge Roko Sherry Chayat, American Rinzai Zen teacher and abbot of the Zen Studies Society (Dai Bosatsu Zendo and New York Zendo).

specials.title: Subtle Sound: The Zen Teachings of Maurine Stuart (editor)

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.tagline: Awareness, the joy of living, and what happens when we die.
Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.bio: Tibetan Kagyu and Nyingma teacher who founded Tergar, known for pairing meditation instruction with neuroscience and for a years-long wandering retreat.

The 14th Dalai Lama.bio: Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, a Gelug monk and scholar who has taught compassion and secular ethics worldwide from exile in Dharamsala.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche.tagline: Essence love, handshake practice and open awareness.
Tsoknyi Rinpoche.bio: Tibetan Drukpa Kagyu and Nyingma teacher, son of Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, whose teaching on essence love and the subtle body works with modern stress.

Tara Brach.tagline: Radical acceptance and the RAIN practice.
Tara Brach.bio: American psychologist and Insight meditation teacher who founded the Insight Meditation Community of Washington.

Jack Kornfield.tagline: Heart-centred insight practice for ordinary life.
Jack Kornfield.bio: American teacher who trained as a monk under Ajahn Chah and Mahasi Sayadaw, co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Spirit Rock.

Gil Fronsdal.tagline: Plain-spoken mindfulness and the path to freedom.
Gil Fronsdal.bio: Insight and Sōtō Zen-trained teacher who leads the Insight Meditation Center in Redwood City and translated the Dhammapada.

Joseph Goldstein.bio: American Insight meditation teacher and co-founder of the Insight Meditation Society in Barre, Massachusetts.

specials.title: Mindfulness: A Practical Guide to Awakening

Sharon Salzberg.bio: American teacher and co-founder of the Insight Meditation Society, best known for bringing mettā (lovingkindness) practice to the West.

S. N. Goenka.bio: Burmese-Indian lay teacher in the lineage of U Ba Khin whose ten-day vipassanā courses spread worldwide.

Justin Sledge.bio: Historian of philosophy and religion who presents ESOTERICA, a channel on the history of mysticism, Gnosticism and Hermeticism.

specials.title: Being and Logos: Introduction to Middle Platonism

Filip Holm.bio: Swedish scholar of religion and educator who runs Let's Talk Religion, long-form videos on mysticism across traditions.

John Vervaeke.bio: Cognitive scientist at the University of Toronto whose lecture series traces wisdom from Socrates and Plato through Gnosis and Neoplatonism.

Charles Stang.bio: Harvard Divinity School scholar of early Christian mysticism, heard here in dialogue with John Vervaeke on daimons and the higher self.

Gregory B. Sadler.bio: Philosophy educator whose short 'Core Concepts' lectures walk through Plato's dialogues passage by passage.

Pierre Grimes.bio: Platonist philosopher and founder of the Noetic Society, who read Plato, Plotinus and Proclus as a living practice he called philosophical midwifery.

Michael Sugrue.bio: American historian whose Great Minds lectures on Plato and the Western canon became widely watched online.

specials.title: Great Minds of the Western Intellectual Tradition

Eric Steinhart.bio: Philosophy professor whose short lectures explain Plotinus' One, emanation and the soul's fall and return.

Denis Robichaud.bio: Historian of Renaissance philosophy and author of a study of Ficino's Plato, speaking at the Lumen Christi Institute.

specials.title: Plato's Persona: Marsilio Ficino, Renaissance Humanism, and Platonic Traditions

Richard Rohr.bio: Franciscan friar and founder of the Center for Action and Contemplation, teaching the contemplative mind and the Universal Christ.

Cynthia Bourgeault.bio: Episcopal priest and teacher of Centering Prayer and Wisdom Christianity who draws openly on Gurdjieff's Work.

specials.title: The Holy Trinity and the Law of Three

Barbara A. Holmes.bio: Writer and teacher on African American mysticism and contemplative practice, a CAC core faculty member.

specials.title: Joy Unspeakable: Contemplative Practices of the Black Church

Theodore Nottingham.bio: Author and teacher who presents Gurdjieff's Fourth Way alongside the Christian contemplative tradition on his own channel.

specials.title: Fourth Way and inner Christianity talks

Jacob Needleman.bio: Philosopher at San Francisco State and long-time member of the Gurdjieff Work, writer on lost Christianity and the inner life.

Gary Lachman.bio: Writer on consciousness and the Western esoteric tradition, author of studies of Ouspensky, Steiner and Blavatsky.

specials.title: In Search of P. D. Ouspensky
Rudolf Steiner: An Introduction to His Life and Work

Mitch Horowitz.bio: Historian of alternative spirituality and writer on New Thought, Gnosticism and Gurdjieff.

Pablo Sender.bio: Theosophical Society speaker and author who teaches Blavatsky's approach to meditation and the inner self.

John Dalton.bio: Speaker at the Theosophical Society in England and Wales on Rudolf Steiner's indications for the future.

Bart D. Ehrman.bio: New Testament scholar at UNC Chapel Hill who writes on early Christian diversity, including the Gnostics.

Anandamayi Ma.bio: Bengali saint, born Nirmala Sundari in present-day Bangladesh, whose spontaneous states of absorption drew devotees across India for six decades; she taught that all is God and that turning towards God is the one duty.

specials.title: Matri Vani (sayings, compiled by her ashram)
Words of Sri Anandamayi Ma (tr. Atmananda)

Ramesh Balsekar.bio: Retired president of the Bank of India who translated for Nisargadatta Maharaj in his last years and then taught in Bombay that there is no individual doer and that everything happens by the will of the Source.

Gautam Sachdeva.bio: Mumbai-based author and publisher, a long-time student of Ramesh Balsekar, who retells stories and pointers from Ramesh, Nisargadatta and Siddharameshwar in short talks.

Wayne Liquorman.bio: American teacher and former businessman who met Ramesh Balsekar in 1987, published his books, and teaches non-doership through the Advaita Fellowship.

specials.title: Enlightenment Is Not What You Think

Sri Ranjit Maharaj.bio: Fellow disciple of Siddharameshwar Maharaj alongside Nisargadatta, who taught in Bombay and in Europe late in life that everything is illusion and only the Self is real.

Stephen Wolinsky.bio: American psychologist and writer who sat with Nisargadatta Maharaj in 1979–81 and later made the film Rays of the Absolute about his legacy.

specials.title: Rays of the Absolute (film, with Science and Nonduality)

S. K. Mullarpattan.bio: One of the main interpreters at Nisargadatta Maharaj's Bombay talks, interviewed in Rays of the Absolute.

Dr. Vanaja Narayanswamy.bio: Disciple of Nisargadatta Maharaj interviewed in Rays of the Absolute.

Atmananda (Blanca Schlamm).bio: Austrian-born pianist who lived with Anandamayi Ma for decades as a brahmacharini and translated her sayings into English; interviewed in 1981.

Swami Chidananda.bio: Successor of Swami Sivananda as president of the Divine Life Society in Rishikesh and a close friend of Anandamayi Ma.

Swami Kedarnath.bio: Monk of Sri Sri Mata Anandamayi Peeth, Indore, who explains Anandamayi Ma's teaching in English.

Swami Vijayananda.bio: French physician (born Adolphe Weintrob) who came to Anandamayi Ma in 1951 and lived as a monk in her ashrams for nearly sixty years.

specials.title: A French Doctor in the Himalayas

Shunyamurti.bio: Teacher and founder of the Sat Yoga Institute in Costa Rica; here he reads Yogananda's account of meeting Anandamayi Ma.

Ajahn Jayasāro.bio: English-born monk of Ajahn Chah's line, former abbot of Wat Pah Nanachat, who teaches widely in Thai.
Ajahn Jayasāro.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Viradhammo.bio: Canadian-born disciple of Ajahn Chah and abbot of Tisarana Monastery in Ontario.
Ajahn Viradhammo.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Sucitto.bio: English monk who trained with Ajahn Sumedho and was long abbot of Cittaviveka.
Ajahn Sucitto.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Sayadaw U Paṇḍita.bio: Strict successor in the Mahasi line who trained many Western insight teachers.

Sayadaw U Tejaniya.bio: Burmese teacher known for a gentle 'awareness of the mind' style of insight practice.

Bhante Henepola Gunaratana.bio: Sri Lankan monk, author of Mindfulness in Plain English and founder of the Bhavana Society.

Bhikkhu Bodhi.bio: American monk and translator of the Pali Nikayas, long editor at the Buddhist Publication Society.

Lama Thubten Yeshe.bio: Tibetan lama who with Lama Zopa founded Kopan and the FPMT network.

Lama Zopa Rinpoche.bio: Sherpa lama, co-founder of Kopan and long-time spiritual director of the FPMT.

Pema Chödrön.bio: American nun and author, a student of Chögyam Trungpa, resident teacher at Gampo Abbey.

John Daido Loori.bio: Maezumi heir who founded Zen Mountain Monastery.

Alexis Sanderson.bio: Oxford Indologist of Shaiva tantra who read texts with Lakshmanjoo.

Swami Chinmayananda.bio: Vedanta teacher who founded Chinmaya Mission and taught Swami Dayananda.

Amitabh (Trika School of Tantra).bio: Teacher of the Trika School of Tantra, which posts short teachings and guided meditations on Kashmir Shaivism; lineage not independently verified.

Guruji Amritananda Natha Saraswati.bio: Nuclear physicist (Dr Nishtala Prahlada Sastry, 23 years at TIFR Mumbai) who became a Śrī Vidyā guru and founded the Devipuram temple near Visakhapatnam, known for opening Śrī Vidyā initiation and Śrī Chakra worship to all.

Bettina Sharada Bäumer.bio: Austrian-born Indologist living in Varanasi; a student of Swami Lakshmanjoo who lectures on the Vijñāna Bhairava, Śiva Sūtras, Spanda and Netra Tantra and on Abhinavagupta's aesthetics.

Bjarne Wernicke-Olesen.bio: Danish scholar of Śākta and Kubjikā traditions.

Satguru Bodhinatha Veylanswami.bio: Head of Kauai's Hindu Monastery (Kauai Aadheenam) and publisher of Hinduism Today; successor of Sivaya Subramuniyaswami in the Nandinatha Sampradaya, teaching a monistic Śaiva Siddhānta.

Daniel Odier.bio: French writer and teacher of Kashmiri Tantra (Spanda, Kālī practice, Tāṇḍava) and Chan; many uploads are in French, only English ones are kept.

Daniela Bevilacqua.bio: Ethnographer of Hindu ascetics on the Haṭha Yoga Project.

David Gordon White.bio: UCSB historian of religions (PhD Chicago 1988) known for The Alchemical Body, Kiss of the Yoginī and Sinister Yogis.

Dominic Goodall.bio: Sanskritist at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (head of its Pondicherry centre 2002–2011); editor of early Śaiva Siddhānta texts such as the Kiraṇavṛtti and the Niśvāsatattvasaṃhitā.

Douglas Brooks.bio: Professor of religion at the University of Rochester (PhD Harvard) and founder of the Rajanaka teaching, rooted in South Indian Śrī Vidyā as learned from his teacher Gopala Aiyar Sundaramoorthy.

Edwin Bryant.bio: Rutgers scholar of the Yoga Sūtras and Bhāgavata Purāṇa.

Éric Baret.bio: French teacher in the line of Jean Klein who presents Kashmir Shaivism as a non-dual, body-based listening.

Gavin Flood.bio: Oxford scholar of Hinduism and comparative religion; author of The Tantric Body and studies of the Netra Tantra and Śaiva theology.

Harunaga Isaacson.bio: Professor of Classical Indology at Hamburg, specialist in Indian Vajrayāna Buddhism and its links with tantric Śaivism.

Igor Kufayev.bio: Russian-born, Europe-based teacher whose darshans and courses draw heavily on Kashmir Shaivism (Trika, Krama, Spanda) and on kundalini as the process of awakening.

James Mallinson.bio: Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and leader of the Haṭha Yoga Project; edited the Khecarīvidyā, Dattātreyayogaśāstra and Amṛtasiddhi; also an initiated Rāmānandī mahant.

Jason Birch.bio: Historian of medieval yoga on the Haṭha Yoga Project; editor of the Amanaska, Amaraugha and Yogacintāmaṇi.

Kavitha Chinnaiyan.bio: Cardiologist and teacher of Śrī Vidyā and Advaita (Svatantra Institute).

Loriliai Biernacki.bio: Scholar of Hindu tantra (University of Colorado Boulder) writing on women in tantra, Abhinavagupta, wonder and new materialism.

Lorin Roche.bio: Meditation teacher known for The Radiance Sutras, a free poetic rendering of the Vijñāna Bhairava.

Mark Dyczkowski.bio: English Indologist and sitarist who lived four decades in Varanasi; initiated by Lakshmanjoo in 1976; translator of the Spanda texts, the Manthānabhairava Tantra and the 11-volume Tantrāloka. Died in Varanasi on 2 February 2025. Since April 2026 his students Arjun Seernels and Brian Campbell lead the Anuttara Trika Kula Reading Circles.

Mark Singleton.bio: Scholar of modern and premodern yoga (Yoga Body, Roots of Yoga with Mallinson); senior researcher on the Haṭha Yoga Project.

Mary Reilly Nichols.bio: Yoga and meditation teacher formed in Siddha Yoga who teaches Kashmir Shaivism.

Om Swami.bio: Indian monk and author who teaches mantra sādhana and Śrī Vidyā; many talks are in Hindi, so only English uploads were kept.

Paul Muller-Ortega.bio: Scholar of Indian religions (PhD, University of California) who taught at Michigan State and Rochester for 25 years, then founded Blue Throat Yoga (2006) to teach Neelakantha Meditation from the Śaiva–Śākta tradition of Kashmir.

Rajarshi Nandy.bio: Indian upāsaka of Bhairava, Kālī and Kāmākhyā who founded the Kamakhya Bhairava Upasaka Foundation (KBUF); speaks in English, sometimes mixed with Hindi, on Shākta sādhana.

Pandit Rajmani Tigunait.bio: Spiritual head of the Himalayan Institute and successor of Swami Rama; Sanskritist who teaches Śrī Vidyā, the Śrī Sūkta and tantric mantra practice.

Richard Gombrich.bio: Oxford Indologist and Buddhologist; supervised Mark Dyczkowski's doctorate.

Sadhguru (Jaggi Vasudev).bio: Founder of the Isha Foundation; consecrated the Linga Bhairavi goddess form at Coimbatore and teaches Bhairavi Sadhana as a devotional practice open to lay people.

Sally Kempton.bio: Journalist turned monastic in Swami Muktananda's Siddha Yoga (met Muktananda in 1974; initiated as Swami Durgananda in 1982); later an independent teacher of meditation, Kashmir Shaivism and goddess practice (Awakening Shakti, Meditation for the Love of It).

Seth Powell.bio: Historian of yoga and founder of the Yogic Studies platform and podcast.

Shaman Hatley.bio: Scholar of early tantric Śaivism and yoginī cults (UMass Boston); editor of the Brahmayāmala.

Shambhavi Sarasvati.bio: Spiritual director of Jaya Kula in Portland, Oregon, teaching Trika Shaivism alongside Tibetan Dzogchen; Anandamayi Ma is her root guru.

Satguru Sivaya Subramuniyaswami (Gurudev.bio: American-born founder of Kauai's Hindu Monastery and Himalayan Academy, initiated by Yogaswami of Jaffna; author of Dancing with Siva and Merging with Siva.

Sravana Borkataky-Varma.bio: Scholar of Śākta tantra in Assam and of women practitioners.

Sthaneshwar Timalsina.bio: Nepali-born scholar-practitioner (San Diego State University) who teaches Śākta and Śaiva tantra through his Vimarsha Foundation.

Swami Khecaranatha.bio: American teacher in the line of Swami Rudrananda (Rudi) who teaches Trika Shaivism and kundalini practice through his Heart of Consciousness community.

Swami Shankarananda.bio: Disciple of Swami Muktananda who founded the Shiva Ashram near Melbourne; teaches Kashmir Shaivism and his own self-inquiry method, the Shiva Process.

Yamajit.bio: Teacher at the Tridevi Chamunda Mandir who streams long satsangs on the twelve Kālīs of the Krama, the Mātṛkās, the 64 Yoginīs and Vijñāna Bhairava meditations.

Ajahn Brahmali.bio: Norwegian-born monk trained under Ajahn Brahm at Bodhinyana; teaches the early suttas and Vinaya closely, often co-teaching sutta courses with Bhante Sujato.
Ajahn Brahmali.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Bhante Sujato.bio: Australian monk ordained in the Ajahn Chah tradition; founder of Santi Forest Monastery and co-founder of SuttaCentral, where he has published free English translations of the four main Nikāyas.

Ajahn Hasapanna.bio: Monk of the Bodhinyana / BSWA community in Western Australia, a student of Ajahn Brahm.
Ajahn Hasapanna.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Ñāṇiko.bio: Senior monk at Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition; gives many of the monastery's evening and retreat talks.
Ajahn Ñāṇiko.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Karuṇadhammo.bio: American monk of the Ajahn Chah tradition and former abbot of Abhayagiri.
Ajahn Karuṇadhammo.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Cunda.bio: Monk of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.
Ajahn Cunda.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Sudhīro.bio: Monk of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.
Ajahn Sudhīro.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Ahiṃsako.bio: Monk of Cittaviveka (Chithurst) Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.
Ajahn Ahiṃsako.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Karuniko.bio: Senior monk at Cittaviveka (Chithurst) in the Ajahn Chah tradition.
Ajahn Karuniko.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Sona.bio: Canadian monk and co-founder of Birken Forest Monastery in British Columbia, in the Thai forest tradition; known for practical talks on jhāna and daily life.
Ajahn Sona.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Anan.bio: Thai monk who ordained under Ajahn Chah in 1975 and founded Wat Marp Jan in Rayong; teaches weekly in Thai with English translation.
Ajahn Anan.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Kalyano.bio: Australian monk, a long-time student and translator of Ajahn Anan; abbot of Buddha Bodhivana Monastery near Melbourne.
Ajahn Kalyano.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Ajahn Chandako.bio: American-born monk of the Ajahn Chah tradition; abbot of Vimutti Buddhist Monastery in New Zealand.
Ajahn Chandako.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda.bio: Burmese scholar-monk trained in the Mahasi tradition; founded the Theravada Buddhist Society of America and taught Abhidhamma and satipaṭṭhāna in California.

Sayadaw U Thuzana.bio: Burmese teacher in the Mahasi lineage who leads retreats at the Tathagata Meditation Center.

Sayadaw U Nandasiri.bio: Burmese teacher in the Mahasi lineage who leads retreats at the Tathagata Meditation Center.

Bhikkhu Anālayo.bio: German-born monk and scholar ordained in Sri Lanka; specialist in comparative study of the Pāli Nikāyas and Chinese Āgamas, and author of widely used books on satipaṭṭhāna.

Swami Pavitrananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order who led the Vedanta Society of New York from 1951; heard here in archival recordings.

Swami Tathagatananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and long-time head of the Vedanta Society of New York; heard here in archival recordings.

Swami Dhyanayogananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

Swami Medhananda (Ayon Maharaj).bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and philosopher (Ayon Maharaj), author of studies of Ramakrishna's and Vivekananda's philosophy.

Pravrajika Vrajaprana.bio: Nun of the Sarada Convent (Vedanta Society of Southern California) and author of books on Vedanta.

Pravrajika Krishnaprana.bio: Nun of the Sarada Convent, Vedanta Society of Southern California.

Swami Tyagananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order, head of the Ramakrishna Vedanta Society of Boston and Hindu chaplain at Harvard and MIT.

Swami Chetanananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order, minister of the Vedanta Society of St. Louis and author of histories of Ramakrishna's disciples.

Swami Shivarchanananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of St. Louis.

Swami Ishatmananda.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and head of the Vivekananda Vedanta Society of Chicago.

Swami Tejomayananda.bio: Disciple of Swami Chinmayananda and former head of the Chinmaya Mission worldwide.

Swami Swaroopananda (Chinmaya Mission).bio: Disciple of Swami Chinmayananda and current global head of the Chinmaya Mission.

Swamini Svatmavidyananda.bio: Traditional teacher of Vedānta in the line of Swami Dayananda Saraswati.

Swami Tattvavidananda.bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati teaching Vedānta and Sanskrit.

Swami Viditatmananda.bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati, long associated with the Arsha Vidya Gurukulam.

Radhanath Swami.bio: American-born Gaudiya Vaishnava teacher in ISKCON, a disciple of A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, and author of "The Journey Home".

Swami Niranjanananda Saraswati.bio: Successor of Swami Satyananda Saraswati and long-time head of the Bihar School of Yoga in Munger.

Swami Swaroopananda (Sivananda).bio: Senior acharya of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres, a disciple of Swami Vishnudevananda.

Swami Sitaramananda.bio: Acharya of the Sivananda Yoga Farm in California, a disciple of Swami Vishnudevananda.

Swami Paramananda (Sivananda).bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres (not the Ramakrishna-order Swami Paramananda, 1884–1940).

Swami Shambhudevananda.bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

Swami Brahmananda (Sivananda).bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres (not the Ramakrishna-order Swami Brahmananda).

Ajahn Dtun.bio: Thai monk ordained at Wat Nong Pah Pong with Ajahn Chah as preceptor (1978); trained with Ajahn Piak and Ajahn Anan and founded Wat Boonyawad in Chonburi.
Ajahn Dtun.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)

Alexander Wynne.bio: British scholar of early Buddhism; Oxford DPhil under Richard Gombrich, author of "The Origin of Buddhist Meditation", and an editor of the Journal of the OCBS.

Rupert Gethin.bio: British scholar of the Nikāyas and Abhidhamma, emeritus professor at Bristol and president of the Pali Text Society; PhD at Manchester under Lance Cousins.

Steven Collins.bio: British scholar of Pāli Buddhism at Chicago, author of "Selfless Persons" and "Nirvana and Other Buddhist Felicities"; Oxford DPhil under Richard Gombrich.

Jeffery D. Long.bio: American scholar of Hindu and Jain traditions at Elizabethtown College, closely associated with the Vedanta Societies.

T. K. V. Desikachar.bio: Son and student of T. Krishnamacharya; founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in Chennai and taught yoga adapted to the individual.

Wendy Doniger.bio: American Indologist at the University of Chicago, translator of Sanskrit texts and author of "The Hindus: An Alternative History".

Nicholas Sutton.bio: Scholar of the Mahābhārata and Bhagavad Gītā who teaches the OCHS online courses.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche.bio: Kagyu and Nyingma lama, founder of Nalandabodhi, who presents mind training and the "mindful gap" to modern audiences with humour and an interest in art and popular culture.

Ringu Tulku Rinpoche.bio: Karma Kagyu lama and scholar of the Rimé movement, former professor of Tibetan studies in Sikkim, who founded Bodhicharya and teaches in a light, accessible style.

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche.bio: Bön lama trained at Menri under Lopön Tenzin Namdak, founder of Ligmincha International, who teaches Bön Dzogchen, dream yoga and the healing practices of sound and breath.

Valerie Forstman.bio: Associate Zen Master of the Sanbo Zen lineage and guiding teacher of Mountain Cloud Zen Center, first a student of Ruben Habito.

Chigan Roshi.bio: Rinzai Zen teacher with the Zen Studies Society who gives teisho on koan collections at Dai Bosatsu Zendo and New York Zendo.

Jeffrey Hopkins.bio: Scholar and translator of Gelug Madhyamaka and tantra, founder of the Tibetan Buddhist studies doctoral programme at the University of Virginia and the Dalai Lama's chief English interpreter 1979–89.

Lama Jampa Thaye.bio: British-born lama authorised in the Sakya and Karma Kagyu traditions by Karma Thinley Rinpoche, founder of the Dechen community and a scholar of Tibetan Buddhism.

Kwan Um School of Zen (various Zen Maste.bio: The Kwan Um School of Zen, the international Korean Seon school founded by Zen Master Seung Sahn; the channel collects short talks by many of its Zen Masters.

Tendai Buddhist Institute (weekly dharma.bio: Tendai Buddhist Institute in New York state, the American branch of Japanese Tendai; its weekly Wednesday talks cover Tiantai/Tendai doctrine and practice.

Foundation for Shingon Buddhism (classes.bio: Foundation for Shingon Buddhism, which shares Shingon esoteric Buddhism, its texts and Koyasan culture in English.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.bio: Bhutanese Rimé lama of the Sakya and Nyingma lines, recognised as an incarnation of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo; filmmaker, author and founder of Siddhartha's Intent and Khyentse Foundation.

B. Alan Wallace.bio: American scholar-practitioner ordained by the Dalai Lama and trained by Geshe Rabten, later a Stanford PhD, who teaches shamatha and Dzogchen and argues for a "contemplative science" of mind.

Khentrul Rinpoche.bio: Shar Khentrul Jamphel Lodrö, a Jonang master trained in a non-sectarian (Rimé) way, who teaches Kalachakra and the shentong "other-emptiness" view through Dzokden.

Robert A. F. Thurman.bio: American scholar and translator, the first Westerner ordained a Tibetan Buddhist monk, Jey Tsong Khapa Professor at Columbia and co-founder of Tibet House US; died in June 2026.

Master Sheng Yen.bio: Taiwanese Chan master of the Linji and Caodong lines and founder of Dharma Drum Mountain, who revived Chan practice and taught in the West; his Great Dharma Drum TV series answers short questions.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche.bio: Nyingma lama, son of Neten Chokling Rinpoche and former professor at Naropa, founder of Mangala Shri Bhuti, and teacher of Pema Chödrön.

Hokuto Daniel Diffin.bio: Rinzai Zen priest with the Zen Studies Society (Hokuto Osho) who gives Dharma talks on the Record of Linji.

Anne C. Klein (Lama Rigzin Drolma).bio: Professor of Religious Studies at Rice University and, as Lama Rigzin Drolma, co-founder of Dawn Mountain in Houston, teaching Nyingma Dzogchen.

Thupten Jinpa.bio: Former Gelug monk with a Geshe Lharampa degree and a Cambridge PhD, principal English translator to the Dalai Lama since 1985, Tsongkhapa biographer and author of the Compassion Cultivation Training programme.

Jundo Cohen.bio: American Soto Zen priest living in Japan, Dharma heir of Gudo Wafu Nishijima and founder of the online Treeleaf Zendo.

Lama Tsultrim Allione.bio: American teacher, one of the first Western women ordained in Tibetan Buddhism (1970), founder of Tara Mandala and author of Women of Wisdom and Feeding Your Demons, a modern adaptation of Chöd.

Jan Chozen Bays.bio: Jan Chozen Bays, Dharma heir of Taizan Maezumi, paediatrician and co-abbot of Great Vow Zen Monastery in Oregon.

Rev. Meian Elbert.bio: Abbess of Shasta Abbey in the Order of Buddhist Contemplatives founded by Houn Jiyu-Kennett.

Jiryu Rutschman-Byler.bio: Soto Zen priest and former abbot of Green Gulch Farm, San Francisco Zen Center.

Anam Thubten.bio: Tibetan teacher trained in the Nyingma tradition who leads the Dharmata Foundation in California and teaches a direct, non-sectarian approach to awakening.

Phakchok Rinpoche.bio: Nyingma and Kagyu lineage holder, grandson of Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and founder of the Samye Institute.

Guo Gu.bio: Guo Gu (Jimmy Yu), Dharma heir of Master Sheng Yen and professor of religion at Florida State University, who teaches silent illumination and huatou at the Tallahassee Chan Center.

David Germano.bio: Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia, a historian of the Great Perfection (Dzogchen) and founder of the Tibetan and Himalayan Library and UVA's Contemplative Sciences Center.

Barry Magid.bio: Psychiatrist and Dharma heir of Charlotte Joko Beck who founded Ordinary Mind Zendo in New York.

Elizabeth Mattis Namgyel.bio: American teacher in the Nyingma line of Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche, author of The Power of an Open Question, who explores Madhyamaka "not knowing" in daily life.

Lama Lena.bio: American teacher (Yeshe Kaytup) of Dzogchen and Mahamudra, a long-time student of Wangdor Rinpoche, known for informal, precise "direct mind perception" teachings streamed from many cities.

Lama Shenpen Hookham.bio: British Kagyu and Nyingma teacher, Oxford DPhil on shentong buddha-nature, founder of the Awakened Heart Sangha.

Brother Phap Hai.bio: Plum Village monastic (Brother Pháp Hải), Dharma teacher in Thich Nhat Hanh's tradition.

Kokyo Henkel.bio: Soto Zen priest from the San Francisco Zen Center lineage, guiding teacher of Santa Cruz Zen Center, with a strong interest in buddha-nature texts.

Jetsunma Tenzin Palmo.bio: British-born Drukpa Kagyu nun who spent twelve years in a Himalayan cave and founded Dongyu Gatsal Ling nunnery.

Tulku Thondup Rinpoche.bio: Nyingma scholar trained at Dodrupchen monastery, former visiting scholar at Harvard, author of books on healing, the Longchen Nyingthig and the hidden treasure (terma) tradition.

Lama Rod Owens.bio: Black, queer Kagyu lama who completed a three-year retreat under Lama Norlha Rinpoche; teaches on anger, healing and collective liberation and leads Medicine Buddha practice online.

34th Menri Trizin.bio: The 34th Menri Trizin, abbot of Menri Monastery in Dolanji and spiritual head of the Bön tradition, successor to Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (d. 2017).

Lama Willa Blythe Baker.bio: Kagyu lineage holder authorised after two three-year retreats, Harvard PhD (2013) and founder of Natural Dharma Fellowship and Wonderwell Mountain Refuge; teaches somatic mindfulness and Mahamudra.

Jan Willis.bio: Professor emerita of religion at Wesleyan and long-time student of Lama Thubten Yeshe, who writes on Tibetan hagiography, women and race in Buddhism.

Tenshin Reb Anderson.bio: Senior Dharma teacher at San Francisco Zen Center, ordained by Shunryu Suzuki, known for close readings of Dogen and the bodhisattva precepts.

Paul L. Swanson.bio: Scholar and translator of Tiantai at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture, translator of Zhiyi's Mohe zhiguan (Clear Serenity, Quiet Insight).

Donald S. Lopez Jr..bio: Arthur E. Link Distinguished University Professor at Michigan, a historian of Tibetan Buddhism and of the Western reception of Buddhism.

Zen Master Dae Bong.bio: American Zen Master in Seung Sahn's Kwan Um School, guiding teacher at Hwagyesa International Zen Center in Seoul.

Duncan Ryūken Williams.bio: Soto Zen priest and professor at the University of Southern California, author of American Sutra on Japanese American Buddhists in wartime incarceration.

Alexander Berzin.bio: American scholar-translator who studied under Tsenzhab Serkong Rinpoche and the Dalai Lama in Dharamsala and created the Berzin Archives (now Study Buddhism), a large free library of Gelug and comparative teachings.

Brother Phap Huu.bio: Plum Village monastic (Brother Pháp Hữu), long-time attendant of Thich Nhat Hanh and abbot of Upper Hamlet.

Robert H. Sharf.bio: D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor of Buddhist Studies at UC Berkeley, a historian of Chan and Japanese Buddhism and a critic of "meditative experience" rhetoric.

Garchen Rinpoche.bio: Drikung Kagyu master who spent some twenty years in Chinese labour camps, where he trained under Khenpo Münsel; teaches love and compassion as the heart of Mahamudra through the Garchen Buddhist Institute in Arizona.

Sam van Schaik.bio: English Tibetologist at the British Library, author of Tibet: A History, Tibetan Zen and The Spirit of Zen, who works on Dunhuang manuscripts and early Dzogchen.

Brook Ziporyn.bio: Mircea Eliade Professor at the University of Chicago Divinity School, philosopher of Tiantai Buddhism and Zhuangzi.

Geoffrey Samuel.bio: Anthropologist of Tibetan religion, emeritus professor at Cardiff, author of Civilized Shamans and The Origins of Yoga and Tantra.

Bernard Faure.bio: French historian of Chan/Zen and esoteric Buddhism, emeritus at Columbia and Stanford, trained under Yanagida Seizan in Kyoto.

Jacob P. Dalton.bio: Khyentse Foundation Distinguished Professor of Tibetan Buddhism at UC Berkeley, a historian of tantric ritual, the Nyingma school and the Dunhuang manuscripts.

Brother Phap Linh.bio: Plum Village monastic (Brother Pháp Linh), Dharma teacher and musician in Thich Nhat Hanh's tradition.

Ruben Habito.bio: Filipino former Jesuit, Sanbo Zen teacher authorised in 1988 and founder of Maria Kannon Zen Center in Dallas.

José Ignacio Cabezón.bio: Dalai Lama Professor emeritus at UC Santa Barbara and former monk of Sera, who writes on Gelug and Nyingma philosophy, Sera monastery and Buddhist sexual ethics.

H.E. Asanga Vajra Rinpoche.bio: Sakya lama of the Phuntsok Phodrang line who teaches at Sakya Monastery of Tibetan Buddhism in Seattle.

Sakya Trizin (41st).bio: Ngawang Kunga, 41st Sakya Trizin, head of the Sakya school for over five decades and now known as Sakya Trichen.

Sister Chan Duc (Annabel Laity).bio: Sister Chân Đức (Annabel Laity), senior English-born Dharma teacher of Plum Village.

Zen Master Seung Sahn.bio: Korean Seon master of the Jogye order who founded the Kwan Um School of Zen and taught "only don't know".

Janet Gyatso.bio: Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard, a scholar of Tibetan visionary autobiography, medicine and gender.

Steven Heine.bio: Scholar of Dogen and Zen koans at Florida International University.

Taigen Dan Leighton.bio: Soto Zen priest and Dharma heir of Tenshin Reb Anderson, translator of Dogen and Hongzhi, guiding teacher of Ancient Dragon Zen Gate in Chicago.

Dosho Port.bio: Soto Zen teacher in the Dainin Katagiri line who hosts interviews with Zen teachers.

Kenneth K. Tanaka.bio: Shin Buddhist priest and scholar, professor emeritus at Musashino University, writing on Pure Land thought and Buddhism in America.

Dennis Hirota.bio: Scholar and translator of Shinran, head translator of the Collected Works of Shinran.

Peter N. Gregory.bio: Scholar of Chinese Buddhism, author of Tsung-mi and the Sinification of Buddhism, a central study of Huayan and Chan.

Richard K. Payne.bio: Scholar of Shingon ritual and tantric Buddhism, long-time dean of the Institute of Buddhist Studies in Berkeley.

John R. McRae.bio: Historian of early Chinese Chan, author of The Northern School and Seeing through Zen, trained by Stanley Weinstein and Yanagida Seizan.

Charles B. Jones.bio: Scholar of Chinese Pure Land and Taiwanese Buddhism at the Catholic University of America, author of Pure Land: History, Tradition, and Practice.

Laurence Freeman OSB.bio: Benedictine monk, student and successor of John Main, and director of the World Community for Christian Meditation.

Iain McGilchrist.bio: Psychiatrist and philosopher, author of The Master and His Emissary and The Matter with Things, on the hemispheres and the sacred.

Bernardo Kastrup.bio: Philosopher and computer engineer who argues for analytic idealism, the view that reality is fundamentally mental.

Arthur Green.bio: Scholar of Hasidism and neo-Hasidic theologian; doctorate under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis, founding dean of Hebrew College's rabbinical school.

Pir Zia Inayat Khan.bio: Head of the Inayatiyya since 2004, grandson of Hazrat Inayat Khan and founder of Suluk Academy; PhD in religion from Duke.

Omid Safi.bio: Duke University scholar of Islam who teaches Rumi, radical love and Sufi practice through his own courses and talks.

Shaykh Muhammad Hisham Kabbani.bio: Lebanese-American Naqshbandi-Haqqani shaykh, deputy and son-in-law of Shaykh Nazim, who founded the order's centres in North America.

Shaykh Dr. Nour Kabbani.bio: Naqshbandi teacher, son and successor of Shaykh Hisham Kabbani and grandson of Shaykh Nazim.

Baraka Blue.bio: Poet and teacher at the Rumi Center whose series Mirror of the Infinite teaches Rumi's Masnavi and the Sufi path of the heart.

Father Spyridon.bio: Orthodox priest who teaches the Jesus Prayer, repentance and the ascetic teaching of the Fathers in short talks.

Angela Puca.bio: Scholar of Western esotericism and magic who runs Angela's Symposium, an academic channel on theurgy, Hermetic magic and the grimoire tradition.

John Main OSB.bio: Irish Benedictine who recovered mantra meditation from John Cassian and the desert tradition; founding inspiration of the WCCM.

Moshe Idel.bio: Hebrew University scholar of Kabbalah who reframed the field around ecstatic Kabbalah and Abraham Abulafia.

Nimatullahi Sufi Order.bio: Official channel of the Nimatullahi order: illustrated classical Sufi teaching stories.

William Rowlandson.bio: Scholar of Borges, Swedenborg and the imaginal who supported the Kent MA in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

Angela Voss.bio: Scholar of Marsilio Ficino and the symbolic imagination who created the Kent and Canterbury MAs in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred with Geoffrey Cornelius.

Sarah Bachelard.bio: Australian Anglican priest and theologian teaching contemplative Christianity in the WCCM.

Becca Tarnas.bio: Scholar of archetypal cosmology, Jung and Tolkien, teaching on the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred diploma.

Peter Kingsley.bio: Scholar of the Presocratics who reads Parmenides and Empedocles as mystics and healers, and writes on Jung's Red Book.

Tom Cheetham.bio: Philosopher and poet, the leading English-language interpreter of Henry Corbin and of the imaginal in Corbin and Hillman.

Seyyed Hossein Nasr.bio: Iranian philosopher of Islam and the perennial philosophy, a leading Traditionalist author and teacher of Chittick.

Huston Smith.bio: American scholar of world religions, author of The World's Religions and Forgotten Truth.

James S. Cutsinger.bio: American scholar of the perennial philosophy and Eastern Orthodox spirituality, editor of Schuon.

James Finley.bio: Clinical psychologist and former Trappist novice under Thomas Merton; CAC faculty and host of Turning to the Mystics.

Louise Livingstone.bio: Scholar of the heart and Goethean enquiry, co-founder of the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred (2019).

William C. Chittick.bio: Scholar and translator of Ibn Arabi and Rumi; doctorate at Tehran University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr (1974).

Shaykh Nazim al-Haqqani.bio: Turkish Cypriot Grand Shaykh of the Naqshbandi-Haqqani order.

Geoffrey Cornelius.bio: Astrologer and scholar of divination, co-creator of the Kent and Canterbury MAs in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

Elliot R. Wolfson.bio: Scholar of Kabbalah and Jewish philosophy; doctorate under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis (1986).

Daniel C. Matt.bio: Scholar of Kabbalah and translator of the Pritzker Edition of the Zohar; studied under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis.

The Prometheus Trust.bio: UK charity founded in 1986 by Tim Addey and others to keep the Platonic tradition alive as a way of life; publisher of the Thomas Taylor Series.

Medina Tenour.bio: Teacher on Sufi women saints and nature contemplation at the Rumi Center.

Martin Lings.bio: English Sufi author and Shakespeare scholar, disciple of Frithjof Schuon and onetime assistant to René Guénon in Cairo.

specials.title: Muhammad: His Life Based on the Earliest Sources

Rowan Williams.bio: Theologian of Christian spirituality and former Archbishop of Canterbury (2002–2012).

Mary Attwood.bio: Art historian of the Renaissance imagination and director of the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

William Stoddart.bio: Scottish Traditionalist author on Sufism and the perennial philosophy.

Alireza Nurbakhsh.bio: Master of the Nimatullahi Sufi Order since 2008, succeeding his father Javad Nurbakhsh.

Cyprian Consiglio OSB Cam.bio: Camaldolese monk and musician teaching Christian meditation and interreligious contemplation.

Mirabai Starr.bio: Translator of the Spanish mystics and teacher of contemplative practice and grief.

Embassy of the Free Mind curators.bio: Curators of the Bibliotheca Philosophica Hermetica (Ritman Library) in Amsterdam, giving guided talks on its Hermetic and Böhme collections.

Arthur Versluis.bio: American scholar of Western esotericism and mysticism, founding editor of the journal Esoterica and author on Platonic mysticism and Gnosticism.

Patrick Curry.bio: Writer on enchantment, divination and ecology who taught on the Kent MA programme.

Wouter J. Hanegraaff.bio: Professor of History of Hermetic Philosophy and Related Currents at the University of Amsterdam and a founder of Western esotericism as an academic field.

Simon Wilson.bio: Canterbury Christ Church lecturer and course director of the MA in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred (2019–2021).

Frithjof Schuon.bio: Metaphysician of the transcendent unity of religions and founder of the Maryamiyya Sufi order.

Reza Shah-Kazemi.bio: Scholar of comparative mysticism and Islamic spirituality.

Jean-Louis Michon.bio: French scholar of Sufism and Islamic art.

Javad Nurbakhsh.bio: Psychiatrist and master of the Nimatullahi Sufi Order for 55 years (1953–2008).

Bernard McGinn.bio: University of Chicago historian of Christian mysticism, author of the multi-volume The Presence of God.

Guru Yogi Matsyendranath Maharaj (Matsye.bio: Russian-born Nāth yogi who lived long among Nāths in India, received full initiation and guru status, and teaches Nāth haṭha and tantric sādhanā internationally through nathas.org.

Yogi Lakshminath Maharaj.bio: Teacher in the nathas.org community who leads online courses on prāṇāyāma, meditation, āsana and Śiva Sūtra satsangs.

Yogi Allamanath.bio: Teacher in the nathas.org community (tea satsangs and talks on the NathaChannel).

Swami Sadatmananda Saraswati.bio: Chief ācārya of Arsha Vidya Gurukulam, Anaikatti, since 2014 and paramount trustee of Sruti Seva Trust; trained under Swami Brahmatmananda (Baroda, 1986) and taught at Arsha Vidya Kendra Bangalore 1994–2014.

Swami Shankarananda Saraswati (Arsha Vid.bio: Disciple of Swami Dayananda teaching online Vedānta classes and retreats for AVG Anaikatti; ācārya of its Jan–Mar 2027 residential course. Distinct from Swami Shankarananda of Shiva Ashram (Kashmir Shaivism).

Swami Muktatmananda Saraswati.bio: Arsha Vidya teacher (Vedānta-sāra, Significance of OM series) at AVG Saylorsburg.

Swami Sachidananda (AVG).bio: Arsha Vidya teacher and chanter at AVG Saylorsburg (Yoga of Objectivity series, satsangs).

Swami Advayatmananda.bio: Arsha Vidya teacher (Hastāmalakīyam course, guided meditations) at AVG Saylorsburg, 2025.

Swami Pratyagbodhananda.bio: Arsha Vidya teacher whose talks appear on the AVG channel.

Swamini Paraprajnananda.bio: Arsha Vidya teacher whose classes appear on the AVG channel.

Swami Atmaswarupananda.bio: Senior Divine Life Society monk who gives the morning meditation talks at the Christmas–New Year retreats, Sivananda Ashram.

Swami Krishnananda.bio: General secretary of the Divine Life Society for decades and prolific Vedānta lecturer (archival recordings).

KYM faculty (Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandir.bio: Collective teaching uploads of the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram: chanting, Dhanur-dhyāna sādhanā, prāṇa lecture series.

Geshe Lhakdor (Lobsang Jordhen).bio: Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, former English translator to the Dalai Lama; teaches introductory Buddhism and Atiśa at LTWA.

Ven. Tenzin Gache.bio: FPMT teacher presenting Nāgārjuna’s Seventy Stanzas and Sixty Stanzas at Root Institute.

Ven. Tenzin Legtsok.bio: FPMT teacher ("Exploring the Mind Itself") at Root Institute.

Geshe Tenzin Zopa.bio: Gelug geshe teaching Atiśa’s Lamp for the Path and the Wheel of Sharp Weapons at Root Institute.

Swami (Sannyasi) Charanashrit Giri.bio: Founder-guru of Swara Yoga Peeth, Rishikesh; karma-sannyāsin of Paramahamsa Niranjanananda (Bihar School of Yoga), teaching the Śiva Svarodaya since 1993; titled Mahamandaleshwar in recent videos.
